subject: Post-demo: PoV playbook & evaluation approach (Healix Solutions)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Claire Mahoney <claire@healix.com>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@healix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: PoV playbook & evaluation approach (Healix Solutions)

Hi Claire / Jorge —

Thanks again for the demo time today — really helpful to see the three primary intake routes and the sample transcripts. Per our notes, I wanted to share a short PoV (proof-of-value) playbook and two evaluation routes so we can lock the scope and timeline.

Quick recap (from our side):
- Goal: Reduce manual triage for clinical intake summaries by 60% while preserving >= 95% accuracy on key fields (diagnosis, urgency, patient identifiers).
- Constraints: Must run inside your VPC for PHI handling; retention policy = 90 days in encrypted KV; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Proposed PoV structure (3 weeks, hybrid approach):
1) Week 0: Kickoff, data exchange & security checklist, sandbox deployment (redwood private).
2) Week 1: Shadow run on live stream (non-prod) for fidelity; capture edge cases and latency metrics.
3) Week 2: Offline batch eval on held-out set + manual grading for edge cases; finalize rubric and success gates.

Evaluation options (choose one or combine):
- Online shadow: High-fidelity, measures end-to-end latency, live error modes, requires VPC access. Pros: real traffic; Cons: slightly longer setup.
- Offline batch: Faster to grade at scale, good for controlled accuracy measurement, less representative of production latency.

Initial success criteria (draft):
- Field accuracy (weighted): diagnosis 40%, urgency 25%, patient-match 20%, free-text quality 15%
- Operational: 95th percentile inference latency < 350ms, average tokens cost <$0.015 per request
- Business: 60% reduction in manual triage time on pilot set

Attachments: pov-charter-draft.pdf (attached), evaluation-rubric-template.xlsx

Ask: Please confirm (A) preferred evaluation route (shadow / offline / hybrid), (B) any additional success metrics we should include, and (C) procurement timeline / SOC2 point of contact.

If agreeable, suggested kickoff window: Tue 3 May or Mon 9 May (we can prioritize the earlier date if security review is completed).

Thanks — I put Marissa and Karthik on copy to help lock technical owners and the rubric.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: PoV playbook & evaluation approach (Healix Solutions)

Thanks Alex — good summary. A few internal alignment points before we finalize the charter to send to Healix:

1) Rubric & weighting suggestion (we should offer as a starting point):
  - Diagnosis correctness (40%) — exact/normalized match checks + clinician adjudication on edge cases
  - Urgency classification (20%) — categorical match with confusion matrix reporting
  - Patient identifier match (15%) — deterministic matching + fuzzy backoff metrics
  - Free-text summary utility (10%) — clinician rating 1-5 sampled reviews
  - False positive safety signals (10%) — number of incorrectly suggested escalations
  - Throughput & latency (5%) — 95p latency and tokens/per-second for ops sizing

  (Weights sum to 100; we can adjust per Healix priorities.)

2) Method recommendation: propose hybrid by default — start with 5 days of online shadow to gather distributional shift / latency and then run a focused offline batch for statistically powered accuracy estimates. That gives both signal types while keeping time-to-insight short.

3) Owners / tasks:
  - Marissa (CS): coordinate kickoff, clinical reviewers, and acceptance sign-off.
  - Karthik (Eval Eng): implement shadow routing, dataset holdouts, run batch scoring, produce dashboard.
  - Alex (AE): procurement / commercial liaison + kickoff scheduling.

4) Timeline tweak: if procurement takes >7 days for the SOC2 review, we should parallelize offline eval prep (anonymized sample) to avoid blocking.

5) Security note: add security-questionnaire.xlsx to the packet and ask Healix to confirm the KMS/HSM approach and whether they need any on-prem connector. I can take point on the PS estimate for VPC setup.

I'll update the rubric template (evaluation-rubric-template.xlsx) with the above weights and a one-page grading guide. Once Alex gets a route decision from Healix I'll drop the final charter.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Claire —

Per Marissa and Karthik's alignment above, attached is an updated PoV charter that assumes a hybrid eval (5-day shadow + 1 offline batch pass). Highlights:
- Kickoff options: Tue 3 May 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 9 May 09:00–10:00 PT
- Deliverables: daily shadow dashboard, mid-week check-in, final scoring report with per-field pass/fail and recommended thresholds
- Sample rubric with weights attached (evaluation-rubric-template.xlsx)
- Security packet: security-questionnaire.xlsx (we'll need a primary SOC2 contact and confirmation on KMS approach)

If Healix prefers strictly offline we can compress the timeline by a week; if strictly shadow we'll need VPC access and a slightly longer setup (additional day for network review).

Next steps: please confirm preferred kickoff date and assign a SOC2/procurement contact (or loop them into this thread).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—Alex
